# Exercises for external-integration.
#
# Each fixture talks to a service through transport.py, which has no network; the
# verifier replaces transport and the clock with a fake service that fails the way
# PROVIDER.md says it does. The request names one failure. The skill's rules decide
# what happens to the failures the request did not name: which ones are retried, what
# a proxy's error page turns into, and whether a repeated write pays twice.

# Retrying a 503 is the request. PROVIDER.md says what else the provider does: errors that
# will not go away, a Retry-After that can be an HTTP date, and a budget of three requests per
# report. The verifier sends a 401, a 404, a run of 503s and a 429 asking for a day.
[retry-classified] fetch_report fails whenever the reports service deploys, it answers 503 for a few seconds, make it retry | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A proxy's HTML error page decoded as JSON. Catching the decode error answers the
# ticket; the verifier also sends a 503 whose body is JSON, which only a status check
# turns into an error instead of an invoice.
[html-error-body] during last night's outage the logs only said "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" for every get_invoice call, make the failure say what happened | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A retried write with no idempotency key. The fake provider applies the payout and
# then times out; a key made per attempt, or derived from the amount, still pays the
# wrong number of times.
[idempotent-write] finance found an account paid twice for one payout after the provider timed out, fix send_payout and keep retrying timeouts so a short blip does not fail the payout | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A paginated listing read by the happy path. Stopping at a short page, pasting the
# # opaque cursor into the URL, adding a second retry loop over the one http_util has, or
# # keeping whichever copy of a customer came last each look right on the fixture's own
# # test. The verifier serves an empty page mid-listing, cursors with + and /, a customer
# # on two pages, and a CRM that stays down from the fourth page.
[customer-sync] the nightly customer sync leaves customers out of the warehouse, find out why and make sync_customers return every customer the CRM lists | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A retried write where the obvious key is wrong in a second way. A key per attempt
# # or per call, or one made from the order and amount, each looks like an idempotency
# # key; only a key taken from the approved request survives the process asking again
# # later and still lets two real refunds of the same amount through. PROVIDER.md also
# # pins an API version and keeps order details out of the provider's dashboard, which
# # the existing code ignores.
[refunds] support found orders refunded twice after the payment provider timed out, fix issue_refund so a slow provider never refunds twice and a blip still ends in a refund | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A client that checks the HTTP status and nothing else: the chat service answers 200
# # with ok false for a rate limit, a missing channel and an over-long message. Retrying
# # every ok false, obeying a retry_after of an hour, letting an outage escape into the
# # runner that is already handling a failed job, or dropping the alert without a log
# # line are each the natural next step; the verifier plays all of them.
[chat-alerts] nightly job alerts sometimes never reach the channel and nothing in the log says why, make send_alert reliable | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
